title: Make the live-loop audit reachable when it is needed, and stop a killed launcher leaving a billed child alive

history.detail:
PASS: PASS — round 1. Audited 7cae2be with bookkeeping 54f9cf3, main checkout. Sprint file read fresh. Working tree clean apart from the known .vscode file.

The FAIL trigger did not fire. Every requirement was verified by running rather than reading, including the two the criteria singled out.

================================================================
REQ 1 — THE LOAD-BEARING CHECK. PHASE-GATE WIDENING, DIFFED NOT READ.
================================================================

Seeded a scratch state file at complete_ready with a gate-1 PASS, both hashes populated with sentinel values, groundtruth PASS and live_test_rounds 1 — the exact shape a sprint has when it reaches that phase. Ran the live-loop audit against it and diffed every top-level key:

    --verdict PASS                 changed=['history']   protected fields: NONE
    --verdict CONDITIONAL          changed=['history']   protected fields: NONE
    --verdict FAIL                 changed=['history']   protected fields: NONE
    --verdict fail (lowercase)     changed=['history']   protected fields: NONE
    --verdict BOGUS                changed=NOTHING       protected fields: NONE
    --verdict PASS --commit deadbeef  changed=NOTHING    protected fields: NONE
    --verdict PASS, notes omitted  changed=['history']   protected fields: NONE
Only history ever differs. phase, qa1_audit_result, audit_rounds, qa1_audit_file_hash, qa1_audited_tree_hash, groundtruth_result, live_test_rounds and completed are byte-identical after every one, and the phase was still complete_ready at the end. No input reaches the gate-1 branch. Not a FAIL.

THE FULL PHASE MATRIX, because a widening is exactly where a leak would appear somewhere nobody looked. Set the seeded sprint to each phase in turn and ran the same command:
    complete          nothing written, refused
    aborted           nothing written, refused
    dev_build         gate-1 result written (unchanged behaviour)
    qa1_audit         gate-1 result written (unchanged behaviour)
    dev_agreed_done   gate-1 result written (unchanged behaviour)
    liveqa_live       live-loop record only
    complete_ready    live-loop record only
complete is refused, which is the requirement's own boundary and the right one: a verdict recorded against a closed sprint would be a verdict nobody can act on, while verify-publish stays runnable there, and the code says so rather than leaving it to be inferred.

THE GATE-1 TUPLE IS BYTE-IDENTICAL. Compared against 02146ca (pre-sprint-15):
    before: if state["phase"] not in ("dev_build", "qa1_audit", "dev_agreed_done"):
    after : if state["phase"] not in ("dev_build", "qa1_audit", "dev_agreed_done"):

SCOPING IS RIGHT AND IT IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. LIVE_LOOP_AUDIT_PHASES is a separate constant used at exactly one dispatch site plus its own die message. LIVEQA_PHASES is untouched at every other use — cmd_reship, cmd_liveqa, and the "there IS a next retest" wording inside the live-loop branch itself all still key on the narrower tuple, which is correct: complete_ready has no next retest coming, and widening LIVEQA_PHASES directly would have silently changed reship and liveqa eligibility too. Adding a constant rather than editing the existing one is the difference between a scoped change and a broad one, and the comment states that reasoning rather than leaving it to be reconstructed.

================================================================
REQ 3 — DEMONSTRATED BY PROCESS TABLE, AS THE CRITERION DEMANDS
================================================================

Launched a headless role with a fake claude that sleeps, captured the child PID from the process table, sent SIGTERM to the launcher, and looked again:
    launcher pid=20284  child pid=20304
    after SIGTERM -> launcher: gone   child: gone
By process table, not by absence of an error. No orphan, no reparenting to PID 1.

CTRL-C UNCHANGED, verified by construction: `process.on('SIGINT'` appears zero times in run-role.js. Every SIGINT mention in the file is a comment explaining why it is deliberately left alone — Ctrl-C's signal reaches both processes from the terminal directly, and registering a handler would suppress Node's own default action on the launcher. Nothing can regress a path that has no handler on it. The behavioural half of that claim rests on Dev Team's real pty run (a genuine 0x03 byte, before and after), which I did not reproduce; I am recording that distinction rather than implying I ran it.

THE UNCOVERED CASES ARE NAMED, WHICH IS WHAT THE REQUIREMENT ASKED FOR RATHER THAN FULL COVERAGE. SIGKILL is named with the reason it is uncatchable by POSIX definition; Windows is named as having no POSIX signal delivery, with taskkill correctly characterised as closer to SIGKILL than SIGTERM, and the cmd.exe grandchild shape flagged as unverified rather than assumed to be covered.

ONE OBSERVATION, LABELLED AS AN ARTIFACT OF MY OWN HARNESS AND NOT A FINDING. My fake claude is a shell script that spawns `sleep`, so it has a grandchild. After the SIGTERM the direct child died and that grandchild survived — child.kill() signals one PID, never the process group. Real claude is not a shell wrapper, so the billed process is the direct child and it is killed, which is the requirement. But a real headless role does spawn subprocesses constantly under sprint 12's scoped profile (a test run, a git call, an npm command), and those are descendants of claude rather than of this launcher. If one is mid-flight when a timeout fires, it survives. Not billed, not this requirement, and not demonstrated against real claude — recording it because it is the same shape as the problem this sprint fixed, one level down, and someone will eventually meet it.

================================================================
REQS 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 — MET
================================================================

Req 2 — read cold from a real reship run, not from the source: "This commit has NOT been through QA1's static audit -- LiveQA's live test is a different check of different things, not a substitute for one. If QA1 wants to look at this commit, /sprint-qa1 will record a live-loop audit while this sprint stays in the fix loop; it is a record, not a gate, and does not replace the retest below." That forecloses the conflation rather than merely declining to repeat it, and it labels the live-loop audit correctly in the same breath. A reader cannot come away thinking either gate substitutes for the other.

Req 4 — verified in a real scratch run rather than by reading the format string. `--commit HEAD` now prints the full resolved SHA:
    real HEAD:  968014544679902beb32396e4d8c256b86592737
    output   :  Sprint 1: shipped (commit 968014544679902beb32396e4d8c256b86592737). Phase: liveqa_live.
I saw the old behaviour myself — my own sprint 13 probes printed "shipped (commit HEAD)" and I read past it. The same bug in cmd_reship was found and fixed here too, declared as incidental rather than folded in silently, and reship's output now carries the resolved SHA as well.

Req 5 — checked with my own AST walk over print() and die() call sites rather than trusting the method described: zero string constants containing a non-ASCII character. That covers strings specifically, not comments, which is what the criterion asked. NOT VERIFIED ON A WINDOWS CONSOLE — I have no Windows access, and the criterion says to say so plainly rather than let a source-level check stand in for a console check. Those are different claims: the source can no longer emit a non-ASCII byte, which is necessary; whether that console renders the result correctly was established for install.js in sprint 14 and is not re-established here for sprint_lifecycle.py.

Req 6 — package.json 0.1.16, one line.

Req 7 — ran both: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED; ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, 127 OK (up 2, matching the two new orphan-guard process-table tests, correctly skipped on win32). verify-tarball.sh: TARBALL VERIFICATION PASSED, "Installed 0.1.16 (first install)".

================================================================
INFORMATIONAL
================================================================

1. The grandchild observation above, for whoever meets it.
2. Dev Team's own note that there is no permanent automated regression test for the Ctrl-C claim is the right call and correctly reasoned — a pty harness for a one-off confirm-no-regression check buys fragility, and the construction check (zero SIGINT handlers) is what actually prevents the regression. Recording agreement so it does not get revisited as an oversight.
3. Carried, unchanged: the --agents argv budget against Windows' 32,767-char limit; the interactive auth-check ordering from sprint 11 round 1; the baseline-fixture drift, scheduled as sprint 16.

RECOMMENDATION

Ship it. /sprint-dev-done 15, then Pipeman ships and publishes 0.1.16, then `verify-publish 15` rather than asserting gitHead by hand.

One thing worth saying, since this sprint exists because of a gap I hit and could not clear: Req 1 makes the live-loop audit reachable at complete_ready, which is the exact phase sprint 12 was sitting in when I could not record an audit of its reshipped commit. That audit is still unrecorded and always will be — sprint 12 is closed and complete is deliberately excluded, correctly. The fix does not reach backwards, and it should not. It means the next one gets recorded.

PASS: PASS — round 1. Live-tested published npm 0.1.16 against a scratch git repo with real headless role launches. Environment: macOS Darwin arm64, claude 2.1.259, /tmp/fc16live. 2026-09-04. Four billed runs, ~$1.20 total.

Both of this sprint's own deliverables are demonstrated working. The five-profile criterion was exercised for the two it prioritises, and both turned up real defects — in sprint 12's profiles, not in sprint 15's work. Recorded as findings, not held against this release. Three profiles remain unexercised and are named below.

PROVENANCE — VERIFIED BY CONTENT
`npm view fully-completely version` -> 0.1.16; gitHead -> 54f9cf3b26a6e3d3a41fe6221515709ff1cc2dd4, an exact match for last_shipped_commit. Tag v0.1.16 dereferences to it. Zero `reshipped` events. Per sprint 13's documented rule I did the content check as well as the gitHead check: all 56 files in the published tarball byte-identical to `git show 54f9cf3:<path>` — MISMATCHED 0, NOT-IN-COMMIT 0 — and my tarball's sha1 (3f637a32805845224457cef4baf05bbf3cc6a746) matches the registry's dist.shasum. I ran the registry query myself before reading verify-publish's recorded MATCH.

================================================================
CRITERION 2 — THE WINDOW IS ACTUALLY OPEN: PASS. IMPOSSIBLE FOR FIFTEEN SPRINTS, NOW WORKS.
================================================================
Drove a throwaway sprint all the way to complete_ready through the real gates (start -> qa1 PASS -> dev-done -> ship -> liveqa PASS), snapshotted the state file, then recorded a live-loop audit at complete_ready — the exact phase where the window used to shut. It landed:

  "Sprint 1: live-loop audit recorded (FAIL). This is a RECORD, not a gate verdict - it does not
  change the sprint's phase and does not substitute for either gate. Both gates already passed for
  this sprint before this record was made; this adds an audit record for a commit reached during
  the fix loop, it does not reopen or re-gate anything."

The message is accurate about its own limits, which matters more here than usual: this is the branch that could theoretically be used to relitigate a passed gate, and the printed text tells a reader plainly that it cannot.

THE SAFETY HALF, DIFFED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Against the snapshot:
  fields that changed: ['history']
and every gate-read field byte-identical, including LiveQA's own:
  phase complete_ready -> complete_ready       qa1_audit_result PASS -> PASS
  audit_rounds 1 -> 1                          qa1_audit_file_hash unchanged
  qa1_audited_tree_hash unchanged              groundtruth_result PASS -> PASS
  live_test_rounds 1 -> 1                      completed None -> None
A FAIL verdict recorded at complete_ready changed nothing but the history array. It did not reopen the sprint, did not decrement a gate, and did not touch my own recorded PASS.

And the append does not break closure — the same sprint then closed normally: "Sprint 1 closed. Confirmed: QA1 audit, LiveQA live test, user authorization." Phase complete.

This is the gap QA1 hit for real after sprint 12, where an audit it had performed could only exist in a chat transcript. It is closed. Widening the branch to complete_ready is safe for exactly the reason the sprint-7 evidence predicted: the branch writes only `history` and touches none of the five fields either gate reads, so it cannot launder a verdict by construction.

================================================================
CRITERION 3 — THE ORPHAN IS GONE: PASS. MEASURED THE SAME WAY THAT FOUND IT.
================================================================
Launched qa1 headless against the published build, let it run 25 seconds, confirmed the child by process table, then sent SIGTERM to the launcher — the identical signal and the identical measurement that produced the sprint 11 finding.

  before kill:   claude pid=54783  ppid=54724 (the launcher)  pgid=54692
  5s after:      none - child died with the launcher
  30s after:     none still running
  56s after:     NONE - orphan is gone

Sprint 11 saw ppid -> 1 within five seconds and the process still alive at 56. Sprint 12 confirmed the scoped profile changed nothing about it. Both marks are now clean. No survivor, nothing left billing in a repo nobody is watching.

I checked the process table by cwd rather than by name, so the result cannot be confused with the user's several other unrelated claude sessions running on the same machine.

================================================================
CRITERION 4 — THE FIVE UNEXERCISED PROFILES: TWO EXERCISED, THREE NOT. BOTH EXERCISED ONES FAILED.
================================================================
The criterion names pipeman and the dev-team profiles as the two to prioritise "if the run has to be cut short — they are the ones LiveQA named as least safe to assume." I prioritised exactly those. The assumption was unsafe in both cases, which is the criterion doing its job.

FINDING A — PIPEMAN CANNOT DO PIPEMAN'S JOB HEADLESS. MEDIUM.
Set a sprint to dev_agreed_done and launched pipeman headless against it. Clean run: exit 0, 6,278 bytes of parseable JSON, zero stderr, 17 turns, $0.45. Six permission denials, and the decisive one:

  DENIED Bash : git push 2>&1; echo "exit code: $?"

Pipeman reported "Status: BLOCKED" and the sprint remained at dev_agreed_done — not shipped. Its allowlist is:
  Bash(node scripts/run-lifecycle.js *), Bash(python3 scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py *), Bash(npm *)
There is no git entry of any kind. CLAUDE.md defines this role by exactly the capability its profile withholds: "Only Pipeman ever runs `git push`, no exceptions, ever."

The comment at run-role.js:360 states the reasoning, and the reasoning is wrong:
  "- pipeman: git (free under acceptEdits) plus npm, confirmed including..."
`--permission-mode acceptEdits` auto-approves the Edit and Write TOOLS. It does not make arbitrary Bash commands free, and git is invoked through Bash. The same conflation appears in sprint 12's findings doc. This is the third instance in this epic of a comment asserting a permission property the code does not have, and the second I have caught live.

Also denied and worth noting: a `Write` to /tmp/check_hash.py — the working-directory bound holding correctly, consistent with 0.1.13's fix.

FINDING B — DEV-TEAM CAN WRITE CODE BUT CANNOT RUN IT. MEDIUM, AND THE MORE CONSEQUENTIAL OF THE TWO.
My first dev-team-1 launch proved nothing: the fixture sprint was an empty template, so the role correctly aborted with nothing to build. That is my harness, not the profile, and I discarded the run rather than reporting it. I then wrote a real two-requirement spec (create greet.js, create greet.test.js, acceptance criterion `node greet.test.js` exits 0) and launched again.

It wrote the source. Both files were created, and I ran the test myself afterwards: "greet.test.js: all assertions passed", exit 0. So acceptEdits genuinely permits source writes inside the working directory, exactly as designed — that half of the profile is confirmed working, live, for the first time.

But 11 of its 27 turns ended in denials, and they are all the same thing:
  DENIED Bash : node greet.test.js; echo "exit code: $?"
  DENIED Bash : node greet.test.js
  DENIED Bash : node greet.test.js; echo "EXITCODE=$?"
  DENIED Bash : node greet.test.js
  DENIED Bash : node -e "console.log(require('./greet.js')('World'))"
It wrote correct code and was blocked, repeatedly, from verifying its own work.

The cause is that the allowlist is hardcoded to this framework's own files:
  Bash(node scripts/run-lifecycle.js *), Bash(python3 scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py *),
  Bash(node scripts/launcher_test.js), Bash(bash scripts/verify-tarball.sh)
The comment at :357 says dev-team "writes source (covered by acceptEdits alone) and runs the test suite and tarball check" — and `scripts/launcher_test.js` IS this repository's test suite. The profile is correct for this repo and wrong for every other one.

That matters because this framework exists to be installed into downstream projects. A downstream Dev Team's tests are `npm test`, `pytest`, `go test` — never `node scripts/launcher_test.js`, a file that does not exist outside this repository. So under the shipped profile, a headless Dev Team in any real consumer project can write code and cannot run it, and CLAUDE.md's own description of the role is "Starts, builds, tests, fixes." Fifty Mission Cap installs into target repos, which is precisely this case.

NOT EXERCISED, STATED PLAINLY: dev-team-2, liveqa, and master-controller were not launched headless this round. dev-team-2 shares dev-team-1's profile shape so Finding B likely applies to it, but likely is not tested and I am not recording it as such. liveqa and master-controller are unknown. I stopped after the two the criterion prioritised, at ~$1.20 of billed runs, having found a real defect in each — spending more to enumerate further profiles seemed poor value against reporting these two now.

================================================================
WHY THIS IS A PASS AND NOT A CONDITIONAL
================================================================
Sprint 15's own requirements are the live-loop window and the orphan fix. Both are demonstrated working on shipped code, and the orphan was measured by the same method that produced the original finding. Its fourth criterion asks me to run the five profiles and "record what was and was not exercised" — a discovery exercise, not a pass/fail property of this release — and I did that, prioritising as instructed.

Findings A and B are defects in profiles that shipped in sprint 12. Failing sprint 15 for them would be failing a release for the code it was written to test, and would send Dev Team to fix something this sprint did not touch. They belong in a follow-up, and they are specific and small: add a git entry to pipeman's allowlist, and make dev-team's test command project-configurable rather than hardcoded to this repository's file.

I would not want the PASS read as "the headless profiles work." Two of the six are now known not to, in the specific way that stops each role doing its defining job.

================================================================
ON DEV TEAM'S GRANDCHILD OBSERVATION
================================================================
Carried intact through Pipeman with its three disqualifiers (not demonstrated against a real claude process, not billed, not what Req 3 asked for) and its stated trigger condition. I did not test it and am not recording a view on it; my kill test used SIGTERM to the launcher and observed the direct child only. I note only that the child I watched had pgid 54692 while the launcher was 54724, so the two were not in the same process group by pid — which is consistent with a group-kill implementation and equally consistent with the child simply exiting on its own; my measurement does not distinguish those, and I did not design it to. Whoever picks the grandchild question up should not read my clean result as covering it.

================================================================
WHAT I OBSERVED VS ACCEPTED
================================================================
Every result above I produced directly on macOS against the published 0.1.16 from the registry. Provenance was established by my own npm query and a full content comparison before I looked at verify-publish's recorded result. Pipeman's report arrived mid-run and changed nothing: its claims had already been independently checked. The one run I discarded (dev-team-1 against an empty spec) is described rather than omitted, so the two dev-team launches are not mistaken for two data points.

================================================================
RECOMMENDATION
================================================================
Ship-ready. The live-loop audit is reachable where it is actually needed, with the gate verdicts provably untouched and closure still working afterwards; and a killed launcher no longer leaves a billed child alive, measured at the same 5, 30 and 56 second marks that caught it.

Two findings for a follow-up sprint, both in sprint 12's permission profiles and both confirmed live rather than reasoned about: pipeman cannot `git push`, and dev-team cannot run a downstream project's tests. The second is the one I would schedule first — it is silent, it only appears outside this repository, and it turns "builds, tests, fixes" into "builds".

Three profiles remain unexercised. This PASS means the code is ready, not that anyone is authorized to close sprint 15.
